title: Provisioning Runbook Check-in — Dec 2 2026
content:
Meeting: Provisioning runbook & regional capacity sync
Date: 2026-12-02 09:30 PT (30m) — notes by Ava
Attendees: Ava Martinez (owner), Ravi Kapoor, Lena Cho, Marco Silvestri, Sofia Alvarez, Jade (SRE) joined for last 10m
Purpose: quick weekly sync to validate provisioning runbook changes, surface regional pressure points, and align next-week hedging for holiday traffic spikes.

TL;DR:
- Runbook v2 changes (auto-scale hysteresis and prefill policy) staged; basic dry-run passed in staging but some edge failures on enqueued prefill when consecutive model rollouts happen.
- West-EU and APAC-E edge regions show sustained 12–18% higher steady-state utilization week-over-week; requested reservation increase of 40 A100 instances for Dec 10–Jan 7 window.
- Preemption incidents down after scheduler tweaks; still seeing ~0.6% request throttles due to KV-cache warmup on long-chained chat sessions.
- Action: short-term reservation spike for West-EU + targeted cache-prefill for top 20 customers. Owners and dates below.

Observations & data snapshot (last 7 days):
- Fleet-wide GPU utilization: 72% avg (peak 94% during 10:00–11:00 PT on 2026-12-01).
- West-EU (eu-west-3) region: avg 83%, 95th pct 96%.
- APAC-E (asia-east1): avg 79%, 95th pct 92%.
- Preemption-frequency (preemptible pool): 0.9% -> 0.35% after scheduler backoff patch ( rolled 2026-11-28 ).
- Request-level throttles due to cold-KV warmups: ~0.6% of generation requests, concentrated on customers running long-chained-dialogue ( > 8k token histories ).
- Cost note: projected incremental reserved cost for West-EU spike = ~$12.6k / mo (pro-rated Dec 10–Jan 7).

Runbook changes in this iteration (v2.1 - summary):
- Scale hysteresis: up-scaling threshold moved to 68% sustained over 3m, down-scaling only if below 50% for 6m.
- Prefill policy: introduce customer-ranked prefill queue (priority = SLA tier + recent QPS), cap prefix prefill to 8k tokens per instance to avoid KV blowouts.
- Fallback routing tweak: prefer cross-region coldstart to local preemption fallback when latency delta < 30ms to reduce preemption churn.
- Instrumentation: add metric gpu.prefill.failures and tag with model_id + customer_id for easier triage.

Dry-run and staging notes:
- Dry-run on staging with synthetic traffic (mixed short/long conversations): overall OK, but observed race in prefill queue when two rollouts happen within 45s of each other — prefill tasks for earlier rollout cancelled incorrectly.
- Root cause: runbook state reconciliation uses instance tags that are transient during rollout; PR #312 fixes by adding ephemeral-lock key in k-v store.
- Acceptance: need one more staged run with overlapping rollouts (Marco) before promoting. Target: 2026-12-04.

Regional provisioning request (ask to finance + procurement):
- West-EU: +40 A100 reserved (Dec10–Jan07) — reason: sustained higher utilization + expected EU customer holiday send-offs + new enterprise rollout next week (CS-2190).
- APAC-E: +20 A100 reserved (Dec15–Jan07) — reason: marketing campaign in APAC and normal holiday uptick.
- Fallback plan: if procurement misses window, enable cross-region burst to NA with cost-passback metric.
- Finance/Proc links: ENGINF-1789 (procurement ticket).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-provisioning if traffic does not materialize -> mitigation: make reservations timeboxed and add cost-threshold rollback at +14 days post-reservation.
- Risk: Prefill queue race during rapid rollouts -> mitigation: adopt PR #312 and add additional reconciliation delay (10s) plus observability.
- Risk: Latency impact for cross-region fallback -> mitigation: targeted routing rule to only allow fallback for customers with latency-tolerance tag or premium SLA.

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco: run overlapping-rollout staging test with new ephemeral-lock change; post results and logs to CONFLUENCE page (linked). Due: 2026-12-04.
- Lena: open procurement change request for West-EU + APAC reservations with finance cc; include pro-rated cost numbers and rollback plan. Ticket: ENGINF-1789. Due: 2026-12-03.
- Ravi: add gpu.prefill.failures metric to dashboard + alert when >5 failures in 10m. Also add customer_id tagging. Due: 2026-12-05.
- Sofia: run retrospective on last Dec holiday spike from 2025 to extract customer patterns (top 10 customers by holiday QPS) and share notes. Due: 2026-12-07.
- Ava: draft customer communication template for customers who will be affected by temporary prefill throttling. Due: 2026-12-06.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we want to allow automatic cross-region fallback by default for non-enterprise customers? (pros: reliability; cons: potential latency regressions and cost). Tentative: opt-in per-customer flag.
- Should prefill cap be 8k tokens or 6k? 8k chosen as conservative compromise but needs trial.
- How to better detect long-chained chat sessions proactively from request metadata to prefill only when likely useful? Suggestions: sample first 2 requests and compute effective prefix reuse score in routing layer.

Notes from oncall handoff (Jade):
- Oncall saw two KV-cache prefills fail overnight 2026-12-01; both mapped to same customer (CS-2190 test traffic) — manual retry succeeded.
- Oncall recommends a temporary alert suppression for automated retries until prefill fix rolled.

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Promote runbook v2.1 to canary after successful overlapping-rollout staging test (Marco).
- Procurement to confirm reservation numbers by EOD 2026-12-03.
- Weekly check-in same time next week; bonus deep-dive if procurement delivery delayed.

Appendix — quick forecast (simple text table):
- Region | Current reserved | Avg util | Requested add | Window
- NA     | 320 GPUs         | 68%      | 0            | -
- West-EU| 120 GPUs         | 83%      | +40          | 2026-12-10 to 2027-01-07
- APAC-E | 80 GPUs          | 79%      | +20          | 2026-12-15 to 2027-01-07

I acknowledge this doc may be iterated; please add comments inline in Confluence or drop notes in #infra-provisioning.

-- Ava
